text_blocks.snippet: Firstcard is a secured credit builder card designed to help individuals establish or improve their credit scores. Unlike traditional credit cards, it requires a cash deposit to secure the credit line, which can help users build healthy spending habits. By using the card for purchases and making timely payments, Firstcard reports positive credit activity to major credit bureaus, aiding in credit score improvement.

list.title: Secured Credit Card:
list.snippet: Firstcard is a secured credit card, meaning it requires a cash deposit upfront. This deposit acts as collateral for the credit line, making it accessible to those with limited or no credit history.

list.title: Building Credit:
list.snippet: Firstcard reports your payment activity to all three major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion). Making on-time payments can help you build a positive credit history and improve your credit score over time.

list.title: No Credit Limit:
list.snippet: Firstcard doesn't offer a traditional credit limit. Instead, your spending is limited to the amount of your deposit. This helps users manage their spending and avoid overspending.

list.title: Autopay Feature:
list.snippet: Firstcard has an autopay feature that automatically pays off your credit card bills from your deposited funds, ensuring on-time payments and helping to avoid late fees.

list.title: No Interest or Late Fees:
list.snippet: Firstcard does not charge interest or late fees, but it's crucial to make timely payments as non-payment is reported to credit bureaus, which can negatively impact your credit score.

list.title: International Use:
list.snippet: Firstcard is accepted anywhere Mastercard is accepted globally, and they do not charge foreign transaction fees.

related_questions.question: How do I activate my first digital credit card?

text_blocks.snippet: To activate a new First Digital credit card, you'll typically need to log into the FirstDigital website or app and navigate to the card management or activation section. You may need your Application ID or the email address used during application. Follow the prompts to verify your information and activate the card. Alternatively, some issuers may allow activation by phone, requiring you to call the number on the back of the card.

list.snippet: Find the activation section: Log in to your FirstDigital account (website or app) and locate the card management or activation section.
Verify your identity: You may be asked to enter your Application ID, email address, or other identifying information.
Confirm your card details: Double-check that the card details displayed match your physical card.
Activate the card: Follow the on-screen prompts to activate your card.

list.title: Locate the number:
list.snippet: Find the customer service or activation number on the back of your card or in your cardholder documents.

list.title: Call the number:
list.snippet: Use the phone number associated with your account to call the activation line.

list.title: Follow the instructions:
list.snippet: An automated system or customer service representative will guide you through the activation process.

list.title: Security:
list.snippet: Some issuers require you to set up security questions or other verification methods during activation.

list.title: Recurring payments:
list.snippet: If you are replacing a lost or stolen card, remember to update your new card information with any merchants where you have recurring payments set up.

list.title: Digital wallets:
list.snippet: Consider adding your new card to digital wallets like Apple Pay or Google Pay for convenient and secure transactions.
